title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Company Personnel
tiers.description: Directors, employees, consultants, contractors and advisors of the Company and its related bodies corporate. Bound by the General Prohibition, the 'front page' test and the Derivatives and Hedging rules; those who are not Designated Personnel may Trade at any time provided they hold no Inside Information.

tiers.name: Designated Personnel
tiers.description: Company Personnel who by seniority or position are likely to become involved with key financial, operational and strategic price-sensitive information: Directors, executives in regional management positions and above, financial professionals involved in preparing statutory accounts, and all head office corporate personnel. The Managing Director may add others. Confined to Approved Trading Periods and subject to the notice, margin loan, speculative trading and short selling bans.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of the Company, a subset of Designated Personnel, distinguished only for the notice regime (a director informs the Chair; the Chair informs the Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Committee) and for the notifiable interest disclosure to the Company Secretary within 2 business days.

tiers.name: Connected Persons
tiers.description: Spouse or partner; dependant children of the person or their spouse; other dependants; anyone else in the person's family whom the person may be expected to influence or be influenced by in dealings with Securities; and a company, trust or entity that the person or any of their Connected Persons controls. All rules of the policy apply to them and Company Personnel must ensure they abide by it.

definitions.hedging_definition: Derivatives ... includes the following if they relate to or derive their value from Securities: put or call options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depositary receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars, and any other hedging or investment arrangement.

windows.start_anchor: the business day after the day full year results are announced
the business day after the day half year results are announced
the business day after the Company's annual general meeting
any other period as determined by the Board from time to time

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: No express power to impose additional blackouts. The Board may only add further Approved Trading Periods ('any other period as determined by the Board from time to time'), and the Managing Director may determine additional officers or persons to whom the policy applies, which can bring a person within the Approved Trading Period regime.

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no venue limit and no approval route, on any use of Derivatives over unvested Equity Interests by Company Personnel holding them and by their Connected Persons. Derivatives is defined to include put and call options and 'caps and collars', so a collar over unvested shares, options or performance rights is squarely caught.
rules.evidence: Company Personnel with Equity Interests and their Connected Persons are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested Company's Securities in any way.

rules.detail: Company Personnel who are not Designated Personnel may use Derivatives, including OTC puts, calls and collars, over vested Company Securities subject only to the General Prohibition, the 'front page' test and the balance of the policy. No notice or approval is required of them.
rules.evidence: Company Personnel and their Connected Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company's Securities, provided any Trading complies with the balance of this policy.

rules.detail: Derivatives over vested Securities are expressly allowed, but for Designated Personnel entry into the derivative is Trading that must occur inside an Approved Trading Period and requires prior approval from the Managing Director and Company Secretary, plus written confirmation to the Company Secretary within 2 business days of completion.
rules.evidence: Other Designated Personnel of the Company must seek approval from the Managing Director and Company Secretary prior to them or their Connected Persons undertaking the Trade.

rules.detail: A director may enter a Derivative over vested Securities in an Approved Trading Period after informing the Chair (the Chair informs the Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Committee); no approval is required, only prior notice, followed by written advice to the Company Secretary within 2 business days for ASX notification within 5 business days.
rules.evidence: A director of the Company must inform the Chair prior to them or their Connected Persons undertaking the Trade;

rules.detail: The rationale given is that hedging unvested equity would allow value to be realised even if performance hurdles are not met and would break the connection between staff performance and shareholder interests. 'Any other hedging or investment arrangement' falls within the defined term Derivatives, so the ban is not limited to listed instruments.
rules.evidence: The use of Derivatives over unvested Company's Securities may allow value to be realised from those Securities even if performance hurdles have not been met. This would break the intended connection between staff performance and shareholder best interests.

rules.detail: Hedging of vested Securities is expressly permitted rather than merely unaddressed, because 'any other hedging or investment arrangement' is a Derivative and section 7 permits Derivatives over vested Securities. Subject to Approved Trading Periods, prior approval or notice, the speculative trading ban and the 'front page' test.
rules.evidence: Company Personnel and their Connected Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company's Securities, provided any Trading complies with the balance of this policy.

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, structured financial product or collar is within the definition of Derivatives and its entry is Trading (an agreement to sell or grant an option), so it is permitted over vested Securities but only in an Approved Trading Period with prior approval. Note that a short-dated forward risks being caught by the speculative trading ban, which names forward contracts as short term Trading.
rules.evidence: Trading means taking part in any transaction associated with applying for, buying, acquiring, selling, disposing, granting an option, converting, assigning rights to buy, sell or subscribe for, or agreeing to do any of these things

rules.detail: Any monetisation of unvested Equity Interests would be effected through a Derivative (forward, structured financial product, collar or 'any other hedging or investment arrangement') and is therefore banned outright.
rules.evidence: Company Personnel with Equity Interests and their Connected Persons are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested Company's Securities in any way.

rules.detail: Outright ban on Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons. The policy defines short selling narrowly as borrowing a security and selling it in the hope of buying it back lower, so a covered collar over shares actually held is not short selling on the policy's own definition.
rules.evidence: Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons must not engage in short selling of the Company's securities.

rules.detail: Section 10 is directed only at Designated Personnel; Company Personnel who are not Designated Personnel are not covered by an express short selling ban.
Securities lending is not named anywhere and is not within the definition of Trading. Borrowing securities is mentioned only descriptively in explaining what short selling is.

Contracts for difference and spread bets are expressly named as Derivatives. They are permitted in principle over vested Securities under section 7, but in practice a CFD over Company Securities is short term Trading caught by the speculative trading ban and, if short, by the short selling ban.
rules.evidence: Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons must not engage in speculative Trading in the Company's securities, such as Trading on considerations of a short term nature.

rules.detail: Flat ban on Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons entering margin loans or any margin lending arrangements in respect of Company Securities, with no vesting-state qualification, no approval route and no exemption. The phrase 'any margin lending arrangements' is broad enough to capture a bank loan margined against, and secured on, the collared shares.
rules.evidence: Designated Personnel or their Connected Person are prohibited from entering into margin loans or any margin lending arrangements in respect of Company's Securities.

rules.detail: Section 8 binds only Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons; the policy says nothing about margin lending by other Company Personnel.

Granting a mortgage, charge, lien or pledge over Company Securities is not mentioned, and the definition of Trading covers buying, selling, disposing, granting an option, converting and assigning rights but not the creation of a security interest. There is no disclosure obligation for encumbrances.

The only financing prohibition is section 8, confined to 'margin loans or any margin lending arrangements'. There is no general ban on secured financing arrangements in respect of Company Securities, and no rule on what happens if a lender forces a sale. Whether a funded collar loan is caught turns on whether it is characterised as a margin lending arrangement.

Speculative Trading is banned, defined to include buying and selling Securities within a six month period and entering into other short term Trading, with forward contracts given as the example. Sale of shares received on vesting of employee incentives is carved out. This makes instrument tenor material: a collar maturing inside six months, or one written as a short-dated forward, is exposed to this prohibition.
rules.evidence: This includes buying and selling Securities within a six month period, and entering into other short term Trading (e.g. forward contracts).

rules.detail: Section 9 applies only to Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons.

clearance.approver: Chair (the Chair notifies the Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Committee)
clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (written confirmation of the Trade; and written details of Trading by the director or relevant interests associated with the director, with sufficient information for the ASX notification within 5 business days)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: 2 business days after completion of the Trade
clearance.evidence: A director of the Company must inform the Chair prior to them or their Connected Persons undertaking the Trade; ... Written confirmation of the Trade must be given to the Company Secretary within 2 business days of completion of the Trade

clearance.post_trade_to: Company Secretary (written confirmation of the Trade)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: 2 business days after completion of the Trade
clearance.evidence: Other Designated Personnel of the Company must seek approval from the Managing Director and Company Secretary prior to them or their Connected Persons undertaking the Trade.
Company Personnel who are not Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons may Trade in the Company's Securities at any time provided they do not have Inside Information.

clearance.approver: Chair for directors' Connected Persons; Managing Director and Company Secretary for other Designated Personnel's Connected Persons
clearance.post_trade_deadline: 2 business days after completion of the Trade
clearance.evidence: Written confirmation of the Trade must be given to the Company Secretary within 2 business days of completion of the Trade by Designated Personnel and their Connected Persons.

short_term.basis: buying and selling within a six month period
carve_outs: a sale of shares received following vesting of employee incentives
short_term.evidence: This includes buying and selling Securities within a six month period, and entering into other short term Trading (e.g. forward contracts).

exceptions.approver: Chair (or, if the Chair is the applicant, the Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Committee)
exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship which cannot be satisfied other than by selling the Company's Securities ... or a pressing financial commitment which cannot be satisfied other than by selling the Company's Securities.

exceptions.approver: Chair (or the Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Committee)
exceptions.evidence: compulsion by court order or enforceable undertaking to transfer or sell the Company's Securities or there is another overriding legal requirement to do so;

Company-initiated corporate actions, such as an acceptance or acquisition of Company Securities under an employee incentive plan, bonus issue, share purchase plan, equal access buy-back, dividend reinvestment plan or rights issue
the disposal of the Company's Securities through the acceptance of a takeover offer or under a court-approved compromise or arrangement under Part 5.1 of the Corporations Act;

dealing in units of or interests in, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme investing primarily in Company's Securities) whereby the assets of that fund or scheme are invested at a third party's sole discretion;

where Designated Personnel or their Connected Person is the trustee of a trust, Trading in Company's Securities by that trust provided that neither the Designated Personnel nor any of their Connected Persons is a beneficiary of the trust

exceptions.approver: Directors must notify the Company Secretary before relying on the exclusion
exceptions.evidence: an off-market transaction involving the transfer or other disposal of Company's Securities between Designated Personnel or their Connected Person and any of the following: a Connected Person ...; a company, trust or other entity over which the relevant Designated Personnel or their Connected Person has control or significant influence ...; or a superannuation fund

instruction of the trustees of the Company Employee Share Trust to acquire or distribute Company Securities on behalf of the Trust for the purposes of ensuring the Trust has capacity to meet its obligations to distribute vested securities to eligible employees;

external_documents: Rules of the relevant employee incentive plan, share purchase plan and dividend reinvestment plan
exemption_authority: Chair, at complete discretion, may grant prior written clearance to sell outside an Approved Trading Period in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court order or overriding legal requirement, or a pressing financial commitment); if the Chair is the applicant, the Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Committee decides. The clearance is valid for seven business days, can be withdrawn on a change of circumstances, lapses immediately on acquiring Inside Information, and clears a breach of the policy only, not the insider trading laws. It extends to selling only, not to entering derivatives or financing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Derivatives has the meaning given in the Corporations Act, and includes the following if they relate to or derive their value from Securities: put or call options, forward contracts, futures, warrants, depositary receipts, structured financial products, swaps, contracts for difference, spread bets, caps and collars, and any other hedging or investment arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both collar legs are expressly within the defined term with no venue limit, so section 7 governs the structure directly: banned over unvested securities, permitted over vested ones.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Company Personnel and their Connected Persons may use Derivatives in relation to vested Company's Securities, provided any Trading complies with the balance of this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is a rare affirmative permission for hedging vested shares, so the derivative legs of a funded collar are contemplated rather than merely unprohibited.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Personnel or their Connected Person are prohibited from entering into margin loans or any margin lending arrangements in respect of Company's Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The ban is not limited to margin loans strictly so called; a bank facility secured on the collared shares with margin or top-up mechanics is likely an 'arrangement in respect of Company's Securities' and would need to be structured, and confirmed with the Company Secretary, to sit outside it.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy contains no prohibition on pledging, charging or otherwise encumbering Company Securities other than section 8 on margin loans, and no disclosure obligation for encumbrances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A non-margin term loan secured on the collared shares is not caught by any express prohibition, which is the key point of difference from policies that ban all secured financing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This includes buying and selling Securities within a six month period, and entering into other short term Trading (e.g. forward contracts).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The collar tenor should comfortably exceed six months and should not be documented as a forward, or it risks being characterised as speculative short term Trading.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Personnel ... are prohibited from Trading ... outside of the following periods: a period of one month commencing on the business day after the day full year results are announced; ... half year results ...; ... the Company's annual general meeting.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Entry, roll, unwind and any physical settlement of the collar must each fall inside one of only three one-month windows a year, and there is no exceptional-circumstances relief for anything other than a sale.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The policy is silent on sales effected by a third party such as a lender, on margin calls and on price triggers.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Neither excused nor declared a breach: lender enforcement or cash-settlement outside a window is unregulated by the text but would sit uneasily with the window regime, so the facility should avoid discretionary lender sales.

bespoke_clauses.clause: If the market was aware of all the current circumstances surrounding the Company, could the proposed dealing be perceived by the market as the Company Personnel or their Connected Persons taking advantage of their position in an inappropriate way? ... Any Trade in Company Securities ... must not be made if that Trade would fail the 'front page' test.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An open-textured veto that sits above the express permissions, so the Chair or Managing Director can decline a collar on reputational grounds even where every specific rule is satisfied.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy also applies to the Connected Persons of the Company Personnel ... or a company, trust or entity that the person or any of their Connected Persons controls.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a family trust or controlled company does not avoid the margin lending ban, the trading windows or the notice requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: It is recognised that in exceptional circumstances, a Designated Personnel or their Connected Persons may need to sell the Company's Securities outside of an Approved Trading Period. ... A clearance is valid for seven business days from the date of the notification and can be withdrawn if there is a change in circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The only out-of-window relief is for a sale, so an urgent collar unwind or restructure outside a window has no sanctioned route.

summary: A funded collar is possible for an ALS director or executive over vested shares, and this policy is unusually accommodating on the derivative legs. Section 7 expressly permits the use of Derivatives, a term that names 'caps and collars' and 'any other hedging or investment arrangement' without venue limitation, in relation to vested Company Securities, while banning them outright over unvested equity incentives. The constraints are procedural and timing-based: Designated Personnel may only Trade in one of three one-month Approved Trading Periods following full year results, half year results and the AGM, a director must first inform the Chair and other Designated Personnel must obtain approval from the Managing Director and Company Secretary, written confirmation goes to the Company Secretary within 2 business days, and the tenor must exceed six months to avoid the speculative trading ban on buying and selling within six months and on forward contracts. The loan leg is the live issue: there is no general prohibition on secured financing or on encumbering shares, but section 8 bans Designated Personnel from 'margin loans or any margin lending arrangements in respect of Company's Securities', so the facility must be a fixed term loan without margin or top-up mechanics and should be confirmed in advance with the Company Secretary. The policy says nothing about forced sales, margin calls or lender enforcement, so any lender sale right should be exercisable only within an Approved Trading Period, and the Chair's exceptional-circumstances discretion covers sales only and would not authorise an out-of-window unwind.
